_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: In the wilderness they were dying, and God told Moses: lift up a sign.
We look to the lifted cross and live.
What the world calls foolish, God has made our wisdom.
The cross is the power of God to save.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son,
not to condemn the world, but to save it.
Come, let us worship the God who was lifted up for us.
We come to the foot of the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: In the desert the people were perishing, snake-bitten and afraid, until God said: look up. Make a sign, lift it high, and whoever looks will live.
We look to the cross and live.
Now lift your eyes higher still, past the pole and the bronze, to a hill outside a city wall, to arms stretched open on a tree.
We look to the cross and live.
What looks like defeat is the power of God; what the wise call foolish is our salvation.
We look to the cross and live.
For God so loved this world that he gave his only Son, not to condemn it but to gather it home.
We look to the cross and live.
Sing to the Lord a new song, for his right hand has won the victory. Come and worship.
We look to the cross and live. Thanks be to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Snake-bitten in the wilderness, the people were told: look up.
We look and live.
God lifted a sign on a pole; God lifted his Son on a tree.
We look and live.
The cross the world calls foolish is the power of God to save.
We look and live.
Come, let us worship the love that gave its only Son.
We look and live. Amen.
